messages:
tom-customer: Hi, noticed our daily usage chart for 2026-03-12 shows zero for the day but the CSV export for the same day has ~14k tokens. Can someone confirm which is correct?

maya-support: Hey @tom-customer — sorry about that. Can you share org timezone and a link to the chart/export?

tom-customer: Org TZ is America/Los_Angeles. Chart: https://console.redwood.dev/orgs/acme/usage?range=2026-03-12 CSV I downloaded: https://dl.redwood.dev/exports/usage_2026-03-12.csv

maya-support: Thanks. Looking at the CSV quickly: the day_start column shows entries like `2026-03-12T00:00:00Z` and `2026-03-12T23:59:59Z`. That suggests the export is in UTC. Does the UI have a selector for timezone?

tom-customer: UI is set to org timezone (checked in org settings). The dashboard previously aligned to PST boundaries. This morning it seems shifted.

sophie-analytics: @maya-support @liam-eng I pulled the aggregated metrics for that org. The stored daily aggregates for 2026-03-12 are empty; we have raw events in the event table with timestamps between 2026-03-12T08:00:00Z - 2026-03-13T07:59:59Z (which is PST 00:00–23:59). The exporter job uses UTC day buckets, whereas the dashboard should translate aggregates into org TZs. Looks like the aggregator stopped applying the org_tz offset in the daily job yesterday.

liam-eng: Reproduced locally. The daily-aggregator lambda got a config change at deploy 2026-03-12T00:02:00Z: `AGGREGATOR_TZ=UTC` got merged by mistake. The code previously defaulted to `org.tz` but our deploy pipeline upstream overwrote the env var when `AGGREGATOR_TZ` is present.

maya-support: Oof. So export in CSV used raw UTC buckets (so counted tokens on the CSV rows but day label differs) and dashboard query expects aggregates keyed by org-day (org tz). That explains mismatch.

tom-customer: Is there data loss or just a labeling/aggregation mismatch?

liam-eng: No data lost. Raw events are intact. Two problems: 1) daily aggregates for org-aligned days are empty for that calendar date because aggregator used UTC buckets; 2) exports pulled the UTC buckets, so they show counts for different day labels. We can recompute aggregates for affected dates.

sophie-analytics: Agreed. Plan: run backfill for org `acme` for date range 2026-03-11 to 2026-03-13. Backfill script will read raw events and aggregate using org.tz. Expect ~5–10 min runtime and will write to `daily_usage_v2`.

liam-eng: Quick mitigation: I'm pushing a hotfix to remove AGGREGATOR_TZ override and default to `org.tz` in the job. Deploying patch now. PR: https://git.redwood.dev/r/redwood/daily-aggregator/pulls/432

deploy-bot: deploy-started daily-aggregator rollback-protected by canary. deploy id dpl_20260312_8a7

maya-support: Thanks @liam-eng. Tom, once deploy is up and backfill completes I'll DM you the regenerated CSV and confirm dashboard matches. Will also add an alert for AGGREGATOR_TZ drift.

tom-customer: Appreciate the fast turnaround. One ask: can you include both UTC and org-day columns in exported CSVs so we can cross-check in future?

sophie-analytics: Good idea. We'll add `day_start_utc` + `day_start_org` to exports. Filing ticket: https://tickets.redwood.dev/INC-9876

liam-eng: Deploy succeeded, canary healthy. Backfill started (job id bf_554). ETA ~7m.

deploy-bot: deploy-complete daily-aggregator dpl_20260312_8a7 :thumbsup:

liam-eng: Backfill done. Verified totals now match: dashboard 14012 tokens for 2026-03-12, CSV regenerated and uploaded: https://dl.redwood.dev/exports/usage_acme_2026-03-12_v2.csv

maya-support: @tom-customer I pushed the new CSV to your support email and updated the ticket. Please confirm on your end.

tom-customer: Got it, confirming now. Looks good. Thanks everyone! :tada:
